May the compiler overwrite

You will learn

How five facts decide whether t27c compile may write its output over a file that is already there.

Without -o, t27c compile writes its output next to the spec. On the lab, measured on 2026-10-18, it did so over a hand-written line, and with -o naming the spec itself it replaced the spec with its own output. output_check decides in a fixed order: the output path is the spec, refuse; no file there, write; -o named the path, write; the file cannot be read, refuse; the generated marker within the head of 5 lines, write; otherwise refuse as hand-written. output_check_today is the unsafe answer the lab measured: write whatever is there.

Try it

Start from the hand-written file and tick -o names this path. Then mark the file as generated on line 2.

Open the interactive lesson →

Without -o, t27c compile writes its output next to the spec, once over a hand-written line and once over the spec itself. Five facts decide whether it may write; output_check answers.

specs/compiler/compile_output.t27

// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
; specs/compiler/compile_output.t27 -- when `t27c compile <spec>` may write its output file.
; gHashTag/t27#10457, follow-up B. Measured on the Railway lab with t27c 0.5.2 built from master
; 982894c96, 2026-10-18.
; --
; Without -o, `t27c compile specs/x/k.t27` writes specs/x/k.zig (k.v for --backend verilog, k.c for
; --backend c, k.zig again for --backend ml), next to the spec. bootstrap/src/main.rs run_compile
; calls fs::write on that path without looking at what is there.
; --
; The gap, as found on the lab (fixture specs/x/k.t27, `module K;`, one passing test):
; - specs/x/k.zig, k.v and k.c each held one hand-written line. `t27c compile specs/x/k.t27`,
;   `--backend verilog` and `--backend c` each printed "wrote specs/x/<file>", exit 0, and the
;   hand-written line was gone.
; - `t27c compile specs/x/k.t27 -o specs/x/k.t27` printed "wrote specs/x/k.t27", exit 0. The spec
;   was replaced by its own Zig output, which starts "// Generated from t27 spec: K".
; --
; What already marks a file as generated: every backend writes "generated by t27c" in its header.
; It is on line 2 for zig and rust ("// DO NOT EDIT -- generated by t27c") and on line 3 for
; verilog and c, below a rule line. In the tree today, 75 committed .zig/.v/.c/.rs files sit next to
; a same-stem spec under specs/. All 75 carry the marker: 14 on line 2 and 61 on line 3. So the
; rule below refuses none of them; it refuses only a file a person wrote.
; --
; The rule, for the one output path a compile writes:
; - The path is the input spec itself: refuse, -o or not. The output of a spec is never its source.
; - No file at the path: write.
; - -o names the path: write. Naming it is the consent; a person who wants a hand-written file
;   replaced says so.
; - A file is there and -o did not name it: write only when the marker is in its first
;   MARK_HEAD_LINES lines. A file that cannot be read is refused (fail closed). A marker deeper in
;   the body is a comment or a quote, not a header, and does not count.
; Out of scope: compile-all and compile-project, which write into an output directory they are
; given, and seal and gen-<backend>, which print to stdout.
; phi^2 + 1/phi^2 = 3 | TRINITY

module CompilerCompileOutput;

/// output_check() answers.
pub const OUT_WRITE : u8 = 0;
pub const OUT_REFUSE_HAND_WRITTEN : u8 = 1;
pub const OUT_REFUSE_UNREADABLE : u8 = 2;
pub const OUT_REFUSE_SPEC : u8 = 3;

/// How many leading lines may carry the marker. Every backend's header puts it on line 2 or 3.
pub const MARK_HEAD_LINES : u32 = 5;

/// The line of the marker in each backend's own header, as generated today.
pub const MARK_LINE_ZIG : u32 = 2;
pub const MARK_LINE_RUST : u32 = 2;
pub const MARK_LINE_VERILOG : u32 = 3;
pub const MARK_LINE_C : u32 = 3;

/// marker_line is the 1-based line of the first "generated by t27c" in the file, 0 for none.
pub fn marked_within(marker_line: u32, head: u32) -> bool {
    if (marker_line == 0) { return false; }
    return marker_line <= head;
}

pub fn marked_generated(marker_line: u32) -> bool {
    return marked_within(marker_line, MARK_HEAD_LINES);
}

/// May compile write its output here? is_input_spec compares the resolved output path with the
/// resolved input path; named_by_o says -o gave this path.
pub fn output_check(is_input_spec: bool, exists: bool, readable: bool, marker_line: u32, named_by_o: bool) -> u8 {
    if (is_input_spec) { return OUT_REFUSE_SPEC; }
    if (exists == false) { return OUT_WRITE; }
    if (named_by_o) { return OUT_WRITE; }
    if (readable == false) { return OUT_REFUSE_UNREADABLE; }
    if (marked_generated(marker_line)) { return OUT_WRITE; }
    return OUT_REFUSE_HAND_WRITTEN;
}

/// `t27c compile` today: fs::write whatever is there. The unsafe reference.
pub fn output_check_today(is_input_spec: bool, exists: bool, readable: bool, marker_line: u32, named_by_o: bool) -> u8 {
    return OUT_WRITE;
}

test a_new_output_is_written {
    assert output_check(false, false, false, 0, false) == 0;
}

test a_generated_output_is_rewritten {
    // a second compile refreshes the file the first one wrote, for every backend's own header
    assert output_check(false, true, true, MARK_LINE_ZIG, false) == 0;
    assert output_check(false, true, true, MARK_LINE_RUST, false) == 0;
    assert output_check(false, true, true, MARK_LINE_VERILOG, false) == 0;
    assert output_check(false, true, true, MARK_LINE_C, false) == 0;
}

test the_lab_overwrite_is_refused {
    // hand-written specs/x/k.zig, k.v and k.c: no marker anywhere
    assert output_check(false, true, true, 0, false) == 1;
}

test o_naming_the_file_is_consent {
    // `t27c compile specs/x/k.t27 -o specs/x/k.zig` replaces the hand-written file on purpose
    assert output_check(false, true, true, 0, true) == 0;
    assert output_check(false, true, false, 0, true) == 0;
}

test the_spec_is_never_its_own_output {
    // `-o specs/x/k.t27` replaced the spec on the lab; -o is no consent for that
    assert output_check(true, true, true, 0, true) == 3;
    assert output_check(true, true, true, 0, false) == 3;
}

test an_unreadable_file_fails_closed {
    assert output_check(false, true, false, 0, false) == 2;
}

test a_marker_deep_in_the_body_does_not_count {
    // a hand-written file that quotes the marker in a comment on line 40
    assert marked_generated(40) == false;
    assert output_check(false, true, true, 40, false) == 1;
    assert marked_generated(MARK_HEAD_LINES) == true;
    assert marked_generated(MARK_HEAD_LINES + 1) == false;
}

test negative_control_today_overwrites {
    // today's compile writes where the rule refuses. Weaken the rule to today's and these fail.
    assert output_check_today(false, true, true, 0, false) == OUT_WRITE;
    assert output_check(false, true, true, 0, false) != output_check_today(false, true, true, 0, false);
    assert output_check(true, true, true, 0, true) != output_check_today(true, true, true, 0, true);
}

test negative_control_a_head_of_two_lines_refuses_generated_c {
    // the verilog and c headers put the marker on line 3, below a rule line: 61 of the 75
    // committed outputs. A head shorter than 3 would refuse a compile's own earlier output.
    assert marked_within(MARK_LINE_C, 2) == false;
    assert marked_within(MARK_LINE_VERILOG, 2) == false;
    assert MARK_HEAD_LINES >= MARK_LINE_C;
    assert marked_generated(MARK_LINE_VERILOG) == true;
}

test negative_control_refusing_every_existing_file_is_wrong_too {
    // a rule that refuses any existing file would stop every recompile
    assert output_check(false, true, true, MARK_LINE_ZIG, false) == OUT_WRITE;
}
